subject: Clarify: Novahub private-offer term ladder and finance acceptance for pilot
messages:
From: Sarah Cole <sarah.cole@novahub.com>
To: karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Cc: Alex Turner <alex.turner@novahub.com>
Date: 2027-01-05T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Private offer options for Novahub pilot

Hi Karthik,

We are kicking off a small pilot to embed Redwood Inference into our customer-facing AI feature. Procurement asked me to confirm a couple of things before we schedule the legal review:

- Can Redwood support a 6-month private offer (pilot) instead of the typical 12-month?
- What approvals are required on our side (e.g., procurement only, or CFO signature)?
- Any recommended packaging for short pilots (prepaid credit vs. term with usage)?

We'd like to move quickly — procurement wants a clear path to sign by 2027-01-12 if possible. Attaching our routing doc for visibility.

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Cole
Head of Product, Novahub
(sarah.cole@novahub.com)

Attachment: Novahub_PO_Routing.pdf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Cole <sarah.cole@novahub.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-05T11:01:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private offer options for Novahub pilot

Hi Sarah — thanks for the clear ask and the routing doc. Short answers up front, details below: 

- Yes, we can support a 6-month private offer for pilots, but it changes the activation and billing pattern we recommend.
- Approval gates: technical sign-off (your platform team), procurement routing (your PO/workflow), and finance for any prepayment or multi-year commits. CFO signature is usually only required for 24+ month deals or unusual payment terms.

Recommended approaches (trade-offs):
1) 6-month prepaid credit: simplest for procurement, no long-term commit, capped spend, faster activation.
2) 12-month term with quarterly usage: better unit economics and simpler for us to provide sustained support/discounts.
3) Staged private offer: 6-month pilot then automatic conversion window into a 12/24-month term if KPI met. Requires a short amendment but preserves speed.

Attachments: Redwood_PO_Template.docx (we use this to map billing and approval fields).

If procurement wants CFO-level approval for the 6-month option, we can offer a smaller prepaid pilot and set an MOU so your legal team doesn't need to craft a long-form amendment. If helpful I can propose the exact language for the DocuSign and a recommended mutual action plan.

Next step: are you able to share the procurement timeline (who signs and by when)? I'll loop Ben for billing activation and Vanessa for approval thresholds.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Marketplace & Strategic GTM
Redwood Inference
karthik_iyer@redwood.com

Attachment: Redwood_PO_Template.docx
From: Novahub Procurement <procurement@novahub.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Sarah Cole <sarah.cole@novahub.com>
Date: 2027-01-06T08:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private offer options for Novahub pilot

Hi all,

Thanks Karthik. Procurement prefers option (1) — a 6-month prepaid pilot — to avoid multi-year commitment while we validate customer impact. Two clarifications: 

- Routing: the pilot PO will need procurement + legal approval; CFO sign-off typically only if spend > $250k. This pilot is expected to be <$75k.
- Can Redwood accept delegated approval (procurement signs with digital signature) or do you require an executive signature?

We're attaching our routing and the proposed SOW. If delegated signoff is acceptable we'll try to get internal approvals by 2027-01-11. If not, we need to know how much extra time to expect for an exec sign-off.

Thanks,
Procurement Team
Novahub

Attachment: Novahub_SOW_v1.pdf

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Novahub Procurement <procurement@novahub.com>, Sarah Cole <sarah.cole@novahub.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-01-08T16:45:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Private offer options for Novahub pilot — proposed path and fallback

Thanks for the quick response — good news that budget looks manageable. Two practical paths so procurement can choose quickly: 

Option A (recommended, fastest): 6-month prepaid pilot via private offer. Redwood accepts procurement delegated signature. We will:
- Issue a private offer with prepaid credit equal to the pilot cap.
- Activation window: 45 days from purchase; unused credit auto-refunds at pilot close or rolls into a follow-on credit if you convert.
- Minimal SOW attachment (we'll push a one-page activation appendix).

Option B (if procurement wants a term but no CFO): 12-month term with monthly usage billing and a smaller upfront commitment (reduces unit discount). Requires procurement + legal but no exec signature.

If you pick Option A I will:
- Generate the private offer and pre-populate the Redwood_PO_Template fields for your PO number and routing.
- Send DocuSign link for procurement to sign (no CFO required for <$250k).
- Loop Ben to confirm billing and Vanessa to set up activation.

DocuSign draft: https://docusign.com/redirect/ABC123-Redwood-Novahub
HubSpot: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/DEAL-2027-0134

Please confirm today if procurement can sign by EOD 2027-01-11 and which option you prefer. If you need a formal statement of work or additional evidence (SOC2, data residency), Ben can follow up with the attachments.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Marketplace & Strategic GTM
Redwood Inference
